描述_ZN: The Falling Woods and Cold Springs" scroll, Qing dynasty, by Wang Shimin, on paper with ink brush, 83 cm in length and 41.2 cm in width.　　On the upper left side of this scroll is Wang Shimin's self-titled inscription: "In the long summer of Kuemao, I imitated the brushwork of Ni Ped's to write a picture of a cold spring with falling trees, Shi Min." Inscription: "Seal of Wang Shimin" and "Seal of True Interest". There are six seals of appreciation: "Sun Yufeng", "once at Fang Mengyuan's house", "Taiyuan's collection", "Xiyi", etc. The six seals are: "Sun Yufeng", "Zeng at Fang Mengyuan's", "Taiyuan Collection", and "Xiyi".　　The year "Kemao" is the second year of Kangxi in the Qing Dynasty (1663).　　This picture was made when the artist was 72 years old, writing about the scenery of Taihu Lake in autumn. The setting is simple, with sparse trees on a flat slope and a thatched pavilion at the foot of a mountain. The painting method is based on Ni Zan, and the rocks and trees are outlined with thirsty strokes, with sharp edges at the twists and turns, but the leaves and small trees are still painted in a way close to Huang Gongwang's brushwork, and the artist's typical appearance in his later years is reflected in his pale and sophisticated style.　　The painting was recorded in the Qing Dynasty in Fang Junyi's "Meng Yuan Book of Painting and Calligraphy".
